topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the course context, and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Clonal evolution and mutational origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary process driven by cumulative mutations that arise from endogenous cellular stresses, environmental exposures, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental versus intrinsic contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the debate and epidemiological evidence regarding the extent to which cancer development is driven by external environmental exposures compared to random intrinsic mutations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral and bacterial infections contribute to malignancy, examining Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study of pathogen-driven cancer.

topics.label: Biochemical mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical pathways through which environmental, dietary, and physical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic factors, inflammatory responses, and host developmental stages establish permissive environments that foster tumor development alongside mutational initiation.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the laboratory, computational, and epidemiological methodologies used to establish carcinogenic exposure and evaluate the cancer-causing potential of various agents.

topics.label: Risk-benefit tradeoffs and lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by framing carcinogen exposure within everyday risk-benefit decision-making and summarising the main themes.
